sources.density_kg_m3: typical value, cf. the rock-density tables of Telford, Geldart & Sheriff 1990 (Applied Geophysics, 2nd ed.) and Schön 2015 (Physical Properties of Rocks, 2nd ed.); rounded to 10 kg/m³; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.erodibility: judgment, relative to granite: weak, fissile mudrock; bedrock ranked by rock strength: river incision scales roughly with tensile strength^-2 (Sklar & Dietrich 2001, Geology 29(12):1087–1090) and lithologic K contrasts span orders of magnitude (Stock & Montgomery 1999, JGR 104(B3):4983–4993); the strength-based contrast is compressed to its square root, so bedrock spans about 0.3–4; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.diffusivity: judgment, relative to granite: soft mudrock; hillslope transport coefficient D of Roering, Kirchner & Dietrich 1999 (WRR 35(3):853–870), used as a linear creep multiplier and scaled by how readily the rock makes mobile soil (soil production function, Heimsath et al. 1997, Nature 388:358–361): loose and friable classes 2–5, soft sedimentary 1.2–2, crystalline 0.5–1; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.vanilla_fallback: P1-28 (Ben, decisions log 2026-10-01): stone stands in for the class: the commonest sedimentary rock: fine-grained, grey, fissile; vanilla has no block that looks like it. The MIC rock-tag README's stand-in was minecraft:polished_tuff; a pack's fallback tags are read first and override this

notes: Grey shale and argillite: fissile offshore mudrock.
